name: Quito
tagline: An Andean capital with a remarkable old town
summary: Set aside a full day for Quito’s historic centre and another for a clear-weather viewpoint. This is a useful mainland stop before a separately planned Galápagos or Amazon trip.
seasonNote: Drier months favour viewpoints; mountain weather changes quickly even then.
arrival: UIO is well outside the centre; arrange official airport transport with a clear destination.
gettingAround: Metro helps some journeys; use booked vehicles for hills and late transfers.
cashTip: Ecuador uses US dollars; bring small denominations rather than large notes.
foodTip: Try locro de papa, empanadas or Ecuadorian chocolate; ask about fillings.
buyTip: Look for chocolate and contemporary craft; avoid protected wildlife souvenirs.
baseArea: La Floresta or a well-reviewed historic-centre property with transport support.

connections.note: Indicative connection; verify actual flight schedule.

sources.title: Casa del Alabado municipal museum listing

reviewSummary: Visitor snapshots give Quito Old Town 4.5/5 with 4,893 reviews and La Compañía 4.7/5 with 5,080 reviews, making the historic centre a strong starting point.

dayClusters.label: A measured introduction to the old town
dayClusters.note: Keep the first day relatively easy at altitude: a central walk and the church interior, with breaks. Avoid adding a high mountain hike on arrival.

dayClusters.label: A clear-weather viewpoint and neighbourhood lunch
dayClusters.note: After an initial adjustment day, use a clear morning for the cable car. Descend before lunch in La Floresta and a craft stop in La Mariscal, using booked rides between areas. Skip the high viewpoint if conditions are unsuitable.

dayClusters.label: Old-town museum and basilica
dayClusters.note: Return to the historic district for two focused visits. Tower ladders are optional; use the lower basilica areas if uncomfortable with height or exertion.
